headline: A paper reports that stronger next-turn metrics did not transfer to customer-support workflow success
summary: Laskar et al. compare gold-history next-action scoring with closed-loop execution on generated multi-turn customer-support workflows. Across Qwen3 4B/14B and Gemma 3 4B/12B, their paper reports that supervised fine-tuning increased average text-turn success by 25.2 percentage points, while tool-turn gains were smaller; the best fine-tuned model completed 8 of 77 tool workflows and no model passed the holistic workflow judge. The result is limited to the authors’ task generator, proprietary workflow dataset, and tested models; it does not establish that turn-level metrics are generally useless.
